changelog: Append a narrow contradiction veto: treat cuts with very-high contra (≥0.90) as effectively catastrophic and rank them at the bottom — addresses the primary finding that high-contradiction signals were underweighted.

Append a short‑latency allowance: permit cuts adjacent to particles or bound‑morpheme boundaries when needed for dense, very-low-latency output, but insist on preserving lexical-word integrity and predicate/attachment coherence — addresses the secondary finding about over-strict bans on internal splits while preventing regressions into word-internal fragmentation.

Replace C3 to relax the categorical ban on internal splits and teach what a GOOD dense cut looks like: allow particle/bound‑morpheme adjacent cuts in very‑short latency when the left fragment is coherent and non‑contradictory and the right fragment can be translated on its own; prefer morpheme/phrase boundaries and avoid splitting inside lexical words.
Replace E1 with measured example ja_jp_1211 to teach scorers to avoid cuts that carry very-high contradiction (addresses primary finding).
Replace E2 with measured example ja_jp_918 to reinforce correct ranking in short/medium latency cases where high-contra cuts appeared too favorable.
Replace E3 with measured example ja_jp_773 to supply a short-latency (≤3) case that showed catastrophic high-contra cuts, guiding safer bottom-ranking of those positions.
Replace E4 with measured example ja_jp_1159 to cover ≤5 latency failure modes and help rebalance against over-ranking high-contra cuts while showing acceptable dense-cut patterns.

Insert a targeted, actionable principle that rescues dense short‑latency choices: allow particle/bound‑morpheme–adjacent cuts conditionally and specify what a GOOD dense cut looks like, so scorers can place dense boundaries without resorting to intra‑word fragmentation (addresses the primary finding about an over‑strict internal‑split ban).
